title: Principality of Vitebsk
capsule: The Principality of Vitebsk was a Ruthenian principality in what is now northern Belarus, created around 1101 when Vseslav of Polotsk divided his realm among his sons and Sviatoslav Vseslavich received the Vitebsk lands along the Western Dvina. It functioned as a dependency of Polotsk through much of the twelfth century, with its princes drawn from the Vseslavich branch of the Rurikids. The principality was drawn into the orbit of the expanding Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the early fourteenth century when Grand Duke Algirdas married Maria, daughter of the last native prince; upon Yaroslav Vasilkovich's death in 1320 without male heirs, Vitebsk passed definitively to Lithuania. The Voivodeship of Vitebsk was formally constituted from its lands in 1508.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's existence and dynastic succession are attested in medieval chronicles, but its precise boundaries relative to adjacent Polotsk and Smolensk territories are poorly documented and largely inferred.
